title: RWB-E1-014 is live in the BRD but retired by D-RCV-60
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 1 v4.docx
description: The BRD lists RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake) as a live Should requirement, while D-RCV-60 and Architecture v5 remove the data lake and read the decision log from events into the reporting read model (ADR-018, decoupling pattern DP-17); the requirement plan retires it with no story. Version 5 keeps the requirement text and records the position in section 8.5 and section 9 of the BRD only.
evidence: BRD v4 section 3.1 row RWB-E1-014 (Priority Should); split_plan legacy disposition 'Retired (D-RCV-60)'; Template and Rules section R6 (retired row) and R5.5 DP-17
proposed: Business owner confirms the retirement and the later home (reporting read model from events) at the next BRD review; the BRD text is then re-worded in a later version, not in this one.

title: Epic 1 requirement stories sit in services whose Architecture v5 wave is later
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json
description: Every Epic 1 requirement carries W-MAP wave 1, while three service epics that receive Epic 1 stories start in wave 2 in Architecture v5: rwb-payment (P8), rwb-asset (S5) and rwb-deviation (S8). Template and Rules section R5.6 keeps the earlier wave, so those stories are built in wave 1; the service still starts in wave 2 for its own epic.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 Services sheet (P8 wave 2, S5 wave 2, S8 wave 2); split_plan legacy wave 1 for RWB-E1-011 (S5 slice), RWB-E1-020, RWB-E1-021, RWB-E1-023 and RWB-E1-062 (S8 slices), RWB-E1-020 and RWB-E1-021 (P8 slices)
proposed: Delivery lead confirms the wave per story at build sequencing; the BRD keeps the business-epic wave and states the rule in section 8.2.

title: Section 3 headings name the ten P modules only, while Epic 1 requirements also carry stories in S5, S8 and S9
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 1 v4.docx
description: The nine requirement headings of section 3 are the P1 to P10 modules of the monolith. Under D-RCV-60 the same requirements also carry linked stories in rwb-asset (S5), rwb-deviation (S8) and rwb-partner (S9). The headings are kept unchanged so that keys and section numbers stay stable; the trace table in section 9 names the primary service epic of each key.
evidence: BRD v4 section 3.1 to 3.9 headings; split_plan slices RWB-S5-E1011-APP, RWB-S8-E1020-APP, RWB-S8-E1021-APP, RWB-S8-E1023-APP, RWB-S9-E1032-APP, RWB-S9-E1057-APP, RWB-S8-E1062-APP
proposed: Renumber the section 3 headings by service epic in a later BRD version, keeping every requirement key unchanged.

title: Four open-decision rows name people in the owner column and no owner role
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 1 v4.docx
description: Rows DL06, DL09, DL12 and DL20 of section 7 carry person handles in the Owner column. The source does not state the owning role, and this run names no person. Version 5 puts the Template and Rules section R9 placeholder in those four cells and keeps the question and answer cells unchanged.
evidence: BRD v4 section 7 rows DL06, DL09, DL12 and DL20 (Owner column); Root AGENTS.md rule 4; Template and Rules section R9
proposed: Business lead states the owner role for each of the four decisions; the cell then carries the role.
